mainTopic: Killing the wrong person according to דבי חזקיה, and a new משנה on convicts who got mixed up: who goes free, who gets which death, and who the 'others' are.
overview: The amud opens at the end of רבי's proof that someone who aimed at one person and killed another pays money. רבא then shows from a ברייתא of דבי חזקיה, comparing killing an animal to killing a person, that this killer is neither executed nor made to pay. That view disagrees with both רבי and רבנן. A new משנה follows. If a murderer gets mixed in with others, all go free, but רבי יהודה says they are locked in the כיפה. If people sentenced to different deaths get mixed up, all receive the lightest one. רבי שמעון and חכמים argue whether שריפה or סקילה is harsher, and whether חנק or סייף is harsher, each bringing proofs. The גמרא then asks who the 'others' in the משנה are, since they cannot be innocent people. שמואל says they are sentenced murderers mixed with one whose verdict is not finished. ריש לקיש says the argument is really about oxen. רבא begins a third answer, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing רבי's proof that 'a life for a life' means money
steps.stepSummary: רבי finishes his comparison of the word 'giving' in two verses: just as the earlier verse means money, so does 'נפש תחת נפש'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'giving' appears in the earlier verse. Just as there it means money, so too here it means money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that began just before this point. רבי links two verses that both use the word 'giving' and concludes that 'נפש תחת נפש' means paying money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the verse 'ונתן בפלילים' clearly talks about paying money. The verse 'ונתתה נפש תחת נפש' also uses the word 'giving'. By this גזירה שוה, רבי says that someone who aimed at one person and killed another pays money and is not executed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Giving'. This is the shared word that links the two verses.
'Here', meaning the verse being explained now

phrases.english: 'Giving' is stated above:
phrases.notes: This is the פסוק 'ונתן בפלילים' (שמות 21:22), about paying money for hurting a pregnant woman.

phrases.english: just as there it means money,
so too here it means money.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְהַלָּן מָמוֹן, אַף כָּאן מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי's גזירה שוה, which began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי, one who meant to kill one person and killed another pays money, because 'נפש תחת נפש' means money.

steps.title: רבא: דבי חזקיה disagree with both sides
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the teaching of דבי חזקיה goes against both רבי and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: what the school of חזקיה taught disagrees with רבי, and it also disagrees with רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes a bold claim: there is a third view on this case. This is a setup line, and the next steps will prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי says the killer pays money. רבנן say he is executed. רבא claims דבי חזקיה holds a third view: no death and no money.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Goes out from', meaning it disagrees with

phrases.english: Rava said:
That which the school of Chizkiya taught
goes against the view of Rabbi,
and goes against the view of the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאי דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה מַפְּקָא מִדְּרַבִּי, וּמַפְּקָא מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי's view, רבא brings in a third opinion that rejects both רבי and רבנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דבי חזקיה hold that one who meant to kill one person and killed another is neither executed nor required to pay.

steps.title: The teaching comparing killing an animal to killing a person
steps.stepSummary: דבי חזקיה compare one who kills an animal with one who kills a person. Neither case depends on intent. With an animal you always pay, and with a person you never pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse puts 'one who strikes a man' next to 'one who strikes an animal'. With an animal, the Torah makes no difference between accidental and deliberate, intending and not intending, or a downward and an upward blow. The point is not to free him from paying but to make him always pay. So too with a person, make no difference in any of these ways. The point is not to make him pay but to free him from paying.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא quotes the ברייתא of דבי חזקיה, which is the source he will use to prove his claim. It sets two cases side by side and draws a rule from each.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whoever kills an animal always pays, whatever his intent was. The comparison teaches that whoever kills a person never pays money, whatever his intent was. Pay attention to the list of cases, especially 'with no intent', because the next steps will focus on it.

phrases.english: As the school of Chizkiya taught:
'One who strikes a man' and 'one who strikes an animal'.
Just as with one who strikes an animal,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא חִלַּקְתָּ בָּהּ בֵּין שׁוֹגֵג לְמֵזִיד,
phrases.english: you did not distinguish between accidental and deliberate,
between intending and not intending,
between a downward motion and an upward motion,
not to exempt him from money,
phrases.notes: The word 'not' isn't written, but it carries over from 'you did not distinguish' just before.

phrases.english: but rather to make him pay money.
So too with one who strikes a person,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא תַּחְלוֹק בּוֹ בֵּין שׁוֹגֵג לְמֵזִיד,
phrases.english: do not distinguish between accidental and deliberate,
between intending and not intending,
between a downward motion and an upward motion,
not to make him pay money,
but rather to exempt him from money.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנָא דְּבֵי חִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that רבא relies on for his claim.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that דבי חזקיה disagree with both רבי and רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of דבי חזקיה comparing מכה אדם to מכה בהמה

steps.title: What does 'with no intent' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case the ברייתא means by 'one who does not intend'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'one who does not intend' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא zooms in on one phrase from the ברייתא and asks what it refers to. This is a setup question for the proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already listed 'accidental', so 'not intending' must mean a different case. Figuring out that case will show what דבי חזקיה hold.

phrases.english: What is 'one who does not intend'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about one phrase in the ברייתא quoted in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact case meant by 'שאין מתכוין' in the ברייתא

steps.title: It can't mean no intent at all
steps.stepSummary: If it meant he had no intent at all, that would just be שוגג, which the ברייתא already listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means he had no intention at all, that is the same as 'accidental'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first explanation and rejects it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Having no intent at all is exactly what שוגג means, and שוגג already appears in the list. The ברייתא would not say the same thing twice, so 'not intending' must be a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say'. This introduces an answer that will be rejected.

phrases.english: If you say it means he did not intend at all,
that is the same as accidental!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין כְּלָל הַיְינוּ שׁוֹגֵג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that 'שאין מתכוין' means no intent at all
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It would just repeat 'שוגג', which the ברייתא already listed.

steps.title: It means aiming at one person and killing another
steps.stepSummary: So 'not intending' must mean he meant to kill one person and killed someone else.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is obvious that it means he did not intend to kill this person, but meant to kill that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning of 'not intending'. It is exactly the case the whole סוגיא is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The killer did mean to kill someone, just not the person who died. Now we know the ברייתא of דבי חזקיה speaks directly about the case where רבי and רבנן disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: 'For this one but rather that one': aiming at one person and hitting another

phrases.english: Rather, it is obvious
that he did not intend to kill this one, but rather that one,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא שֶׁאֵין מִתְכַּוֵּין לָזֶה אֶלָּא לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the first reading, gives the correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'שאין מתכוין' means one who meant to kill one person and killed another.

steps.title: If he were executed, why say he doesn't pay?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא frees this killer from paying. That would be pointless if he were executed anyway, so דבי חזקיה must hold he is not executed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the ברייתא teaches that the point is not to make him pay money but to free him from paying. But if he were liable to be executed, why would it need to free him from paying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the key conclusion from the ברייתא: this killer is not executed according to דבי חזקיה. That shows how they disagree with רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who is executed does not also pay money, so freeing him from paying would teach nothing new. The ברייתא's statement only makes sense if he is not executed, which goes against רבנן. And since he does not pay, it also goes against רבי, who says he pays money.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it teaches'. This points to what the ברייתא says.

steps.whatToRemember: According to דבי חזקיה, one who aimed at one person and killed another is neither executed nor required to pay. That disagrees with רבנן, who say he is executed, and with רבי, who says he pays.

phrases.english: and it teaches: not to make him pay money,
but rather to exempt him from money.
And if he is liable to be executed,
why was it necessary to exempt him from money?
phrases.notes: Someone who is executed doesn't pay anyway, so saying he is free from paying would be pointless.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בַּר קְטָלָא הוּא, מַאי אִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִיפְטְרֵיהּ מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the case identified in step 6 to work out what דבי חזקיה hold about the death penalty.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that דבי חזקיה disagree with רבנן (and with רבי)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's words 'לפוטרו ממון' applied to the case of one who aimed at one person and killed another

steps.title: דבי חזקיה hold he is neither executed nor made to pay
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that, according to דבי חזקיה, one who meant to kill one person and killed another is not executed and does not pay money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we must learn from this that he is not liable to death, and he is not liable to pay money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up its proof. דבי חזקיה hold this killer gets no death penalty and no money payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the גמרא showed that freeing him from payment only makes sense if he is not executed. So both are true: no death penalty and no payment. This places דבי חזקיה together with the view that killing the wrong person is not a capital crime.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it; we can conclude from this
Liable to be killed (subject to the death penalty)

steps.whatToRemember: According to דבי חזקיה, one who meant to kill one person and killed another is neither executed nor made to pay.

phrases.english: Rather, must we not learn from it:
he is not liable to be killed,
and he is not liable to pay money.
phrases.notes: "He" is the one from Step 6, who meant to kill one person and killed someone else.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the final conclusion from the reasoning in Step 7.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: דבי חזקיה exempt one who killed the wrong person from both the death penalty and payment.

steps.title: A murderer mixed in with other people
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that if a רוצח gets mixed in with others, all are exempt. רבי יהודה says they are all put into the כיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A murderer who got mixed in with others: all of them are exempt. רבי יהודה says: we put them into the vaulted chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It rules on a case where we cannot tell which person is the murderer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court cannot tell which one is the murderer, so none of them is executed. רבי יהודה agrees they are not executed in the usual way, but he holds they are locked up in the כיפה instead of going free.

keyTerms.meaning: A vaulted, closed chamber where the court holds certain people

phrases.english: MISHNA: A murderer who got mixed in with others,
all of them are exempt.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
We bring them into the vaulted chamber.
phrases.notes: The כיפה is a closed cell. Instead of letting them go, the court locks them up there.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רוֹצֵחַ שֶׁנִּתְעָרֵב בַּאֲחֵרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is not connected to the דבי חזקיה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A murderer who cannot be identified among others is not executed. רבי יהודה says they are all placed in the כיפה.

steps.title: Mixed-up death penalties get the lighter death
steps.stepSummary: If people sentenced to different death penalties get mixed up, they all receive the lightest of those deaths.
steps.simpleTranslation: All those liable to death penalties who got mixed up with each other are judged with the lighter one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a general rule for when people sentenced to different kinds of death get mixed up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here everyone deserves death, but we do not know who deserves which kind. Since we may not give anyone a harsher death than he earned, all of them get the lighter death. This rule sets up the next question: which death counts as lighter?

keyTerms.meaning: People liable to death penalties from בית דין

phrases.english: All those liable to death penalties
who got mixed up with each other
are judged with the lighter one.
phrases.notes: He means the most lenient of the death penalties that any of them was sentenced to.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל חַיָּיבֵי מִיתוֹת שֶׁנִּתְעָרְבוּ זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a mixed-up murderer to a case where everyone is guilty but of different death penalties.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When people sentenced to different deaths get mixed up, all receive the most lenient death.

steps.title: Stoning mixed with burning: which is lighter?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון says those mixed up get סקילה because שריפה is harsher. חכמים say they get שריפה because סקילה is harsher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those to be stoned mixed up with those to be burned: רבי שמעון says they are judged with stoning, because burning is more severe. The חכמים say they are judged with burning, because stoning is more severe.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the rule of 'the lighter death' to a specific case, and two opinions argue about which death is lighter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree with the rule from Step 10. They only disagree on the ranking. רבי שמעון ranks שריפה as harsher, so he gives everyone סקילה. חכמים rank סקילה as harsher, so they give everyone שריפה.
steps.confusionAlert: They are not arguing about the rule of giving the lighter death. Both accept it. The argument is only about which death is the lighter one.

phrases.english: Those to be stoned mixed with those to be burned:
Rabbi Shimon says: they are judged with stoning,
because burning is more severe.
And the Rabbis say: they are judged with burning,
because stoning is more severe.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנִּסְקָלִין בַּנִּשְׂרָפִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'lighter death' rule from Step 10 to סקילה versus שריפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון says burning is harsher, so mixed-up convicts are stoned. חכמים say stoning is harsher, so they are burned.

steps.title: רבי שמעון's proof from a כהן's daughter
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון argues that שריפה must be harsher, since the Torah gives it to a בת כהן who sinned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון said to them: If burning were not more severe, it would not have been given to a כהן's daughter who committed adultery.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון brings a proof that burning is the harsher death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בת כהן is held to a higher standard, so her punishment should be harsher than that of an ordinary woman. Since the Torah gives her שריפה, שריפה must be harsher than the death an ordinary woman gets for this sin.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to them:
If burning were not more severe,
it would not have been given to a priest's daughter who committed adultery.
phrases.notes: The idea is that a כהן's daughter should get a harsher punishment than an ordinary engaged girl (נערה המאורסה), who is stoned for the same sin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: אִילּוּ לֹא הָיְתָה שְׂרֵיפָה חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי שמעון's position from Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: That שריפה is harsher than סקילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah gives שריפה to a בת כהן who sinned, who deserves a harsher punishment than an ordinary woman.

steps.title: חכמים's counter-proof from the blasphemer and idol worshipper
steps.stepSummary: חכמים answer that סקילה must be harsher, since it is given to the מגדף and the עובד עבודה זרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: If stoning were not more severe, it would not have been given to a blasphemer and to one who worships idols.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים answer רבי שמעון with their own proof that stoning is the harsher death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cursing ה׳ and serving idols are among the very worst sins. The Torah gives them סקילה, so סקילה must be the harsher death. This pushes back against רבי שמעון's proof with a stronger example on the other side.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון proves שריפה is harsher from a בת כהן. חכמים prove סקילה is harsher from the מגדף and the עובד עבודה זרה.

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: "They" are the חכמים, answering רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: If stoning were not more severe,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נִתְּנָה לִמְגַדֵּף וּלְעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה.
phrases.english: it would not have been given to a blasphemer and to an idol worshipper.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אִילּוּ לֹא הָיְתָה סְקִילָה חֲמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי שמעון's proof with a counter-proof for the opposite ranking.
steps.raayaObject: That סקילה is harsher than שריפה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah gives סקילה to the מגדף and the עובד עבודה זרה, whose sins are among the very worst.

steps.title: Sword and strangling mixed together
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives one more mixed-up case. People sentenced to סייף got mixed with people sentenced to חנק. רבי שמעון says they all get סייף. חכמים say they all get חנק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those sentenced to the sword who got mixed up with those sentenced to strangling: רבי שמעון says they get the sword, and חכמים say they get strangling.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of mixed-up cases with one more argument, this time between סייף and חנק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same rule as before: everyone gets the lighter death. The argument is only about which one is lighter. רבי שמעון holds that חנק is harsher, so everyone gets סייף. חכמים hold that סייף is harsher, so everyone gets חנק.

keyTerms.meaning: Those sentenced to be killed by the sword (beheading)

steps.whatToRemember: In every mixed-up case, everyone gets the lightest death. רבי שמעון and חכמים argue only about which death counts as lighter.

phrases.english: Those to be killed by the sword who got mixed with those to be strangled,
Rabbi Shimon says: by the sword,
phrases.notes: He holds that strangling is harsher, so everyone gets the lighter death, the sword.

phrases.english: and the Sages say: by strangling.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנֶּהֱרָגִין בַּנֶּחְנָקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final case to the same argument between רבי שמעון and חכמים about which death is harsher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When people sentenced to סייף and חנק are mixed up, רבי שמעון rules סייף and חכמים rule חנק.

steps.title: Who are the 'others' the murderer got mixed with?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the 'others' in the משנה are. They cannot be innocent people. If they were, exempting them would be obvious, and רבי יהודה would never lock innocent people in the כיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Who are the 'others'? If you say they are innocent people, that is obvious! And besides, would רבי יהודה say about such a case that they put them in the כיפה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking what kind of people the murderer got mixed in with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The obvious reading is innocent people, but the גמרא shows two problems with it. First, nobody would need to be told that innocent people go free. Second, רבי יהודה could never lock up innocent people in the כיפה. So the 'others' must be something else, and the next step explains what.

keyTerms.meaning: It's obvious! (so why would the משנה need to say it?)

phrases.english: Gemara: Who are the 'others'?
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 9, where the משנה said a murderer got mixed in with others.

phrases.english: If you say the others are innocent people,
that is obvious!
And furthermore, in such a case would Rabbi Yehuda say:
they put them into the vaulted chamber?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן אֲחֵרִים? אִילֵּימָא אֲחֵרִים כְּשֵׁרִים, פְּשִׁיטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה is now finished, and the גמרא goes back to its first case to work out what it means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who are the 'others' the murderer was mixed with, given that they cannot be innocent people?

steps.title: All of them are murderers, but one has no final verdict yet
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו, quoting שמואל, explains the case. A murderer whose trial was not finished got mixed in with other murderers who were already sentenced.
steps.simpleTranslation: (Memory sign: ב-ש-ק-ר.) רבי אבהו said in the name of שמואל: Here we are dealing with a murderer whose verdict was not yet finalized, who got mixed in with other murderers whose verdicts were already finalized.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The 'others' are also murderers, but one man among them has not had his trial finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fixes both problems from the question. Nobody innocent is involved, so the case is no longer obvious. Also, locking them in the כיפה is no longer unthinkable, since every one of them is a killer. The difficulty is only that we cannot tell which one still needs his final verdict.

keyTerms.meaning: A memory sign to help remember a list of names
Here we are dealing with (a specific case)

phrases.english: (A memory sign: B-Sh-K-R.)
phrases.notes: These letters help you remember who answers this question: רבי אבהו, שמואל, ריש לקיש, and רבא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Shmuel:
Here, with a murderer whose verdict was not yet finalized,
who got mixed in with other murderers
whose verdicts were already finalized, we are dealing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הָכָא בְּרוֹצֵחַ שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמַר דִּינוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 by explaining who the 'others' are.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'others' are murderers who were already sentenced. Mixed in with them is one murderer whose verdict was not yet finalized.

steps.title: Why חכמים exempt them all and why רבי יהודה locks them up
steps.stepSummary: חכמים hold that a verdict can only be given in the person's presence. Since we cannot tell which man still needs his verdict, everyone is exempt. רבי יהודה says killers cannot just go free, so they are put in the כיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: חכמים hold that a person's verdict is finalized only in his presence, so they are all exempt. And רבי יהודה holds that letting them go completely is also not possible, since they are murderers. So they put them in the כיפה.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל now uses his case to explain both sides of the argument in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under חכמים, the unsentenced man cannot get his verdict, because we cannot tell which one he is. Since we cannot kill one of them, we cannot kill any of them. רבי יהודה agrees they cannot be executed, but since every one of them is a murderer, he will not set them free. He chooses the כיפה as a middle path.

keyTerms.term: אֵין גּוֹמְרִין דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם אֶלָּא בְּפָנָיו
keyTerms.meaning: A person's verdict may only be finalized in his presence

steps.whatToRemember: According to שמואל, the whole argument depends on one rule: a verdict must be given in front of the accused. Since we cannot tell which man still needs his verdict, חכמים exempt everyone. רבי יהודה says killers cannot simply go free, so he puts them in the כיפה.
steps.confusionAlert: חכמים are not saying the sentenced murderers are innocent. They go free only because we cannot tell which one of them is the man who was never sentenced.

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין גּוֹמְרִין דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם אֶלָּא בְּפָנָיו,
phrases.english: a person's verdict is finalized only in his presence,
therefore they are all exempt.
phrases.notes: The step being assumed: we can't tell which man still needs his verdict, and we can't kill one of them, so we can't kill any of them.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
to exempt them completely is also not possible,
since they are murderers.
Therefore they put them into the vaulted chamber.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: אֵין גּוֹמְרִין דִּינוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם אֶלָּא בְּפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes שמואל's answer by showing how his case explains both opinions in the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חכמים exempt them all because the remaining verdict cannot be given without knowing which man he is. רבי יהודה refuses to free murderers, so he puts them in the כיפה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: The argument is about oxen, not people
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a different case for the משנה. With people, everyone agrees all are exempt. The argument is about an ox whose trial was not finished that got mixed in with oxen already sentenced.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: When it is people, everyone agrees they are all exempt. But here they argue about an ox whose verdict was not finished, which got mixed in with other oxen whose verdict was already finished.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the same question from step 15 in a new way. He moves the whole argument from people to oxen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the משנה is about people: a murderer whose trial was not finished. ריש לקיש says that for people there is no argument at all, since everyone agrees they go free. So the case where חכמים and רבי יהודה really disagree must be about oxen that killed people.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא from ארץ ישראל, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
Everyone agrees; no one argues here
An ox whose verdict was not yet finished

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two answers. שמואל (step 16) says the case is about people. ריש לקיש says that with people there is no argument, and the case is about oxen.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
With a person, everyone
does not argue that they are exempt.
phrases.notes: He means people who got mixed up like this. In that case even רבי יהודה agrees they all go free.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, בְּשׁוֹר שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמַר דִּינוֹ
phrases.english: But here, with an ox whose verdict was not finished
that got mixed in with other oxen whose verdict was finished,
they argue.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: בְּאָדָם, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּפְטִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of step 15, which competes with שמואל's answer in steps 16-17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'others' are oxen. An ox whose trial for killing a person was not finished got mixed in with oxen that were already sentenced.

steps.title: Why חכמים exempt the oxen and רבי יהודה locks them up
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say an ox's death follows the same rules as its owner's death, so its verdict must also be given in its presence. Since we cannot tell which ox it is, all are exempt. רבי יהודה says they are put in the כיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבנן hold: the ox is put to death the same way its owner would be, and an ox's verdict is finished only in its presence. So they are all exempt. רבי יהודה holds: they gather them into the vaulted chamber.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of each side in ריש לקיש's version of the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים compare the ox's trial to a person's trial. A person can be sentenced only in his presence, so the same is true for an ox. Since no one knows which ox still needs its verdict, none can be sentenced, and all go free. רבי יהודה does not let them go free, so he locks them in the כיפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The ox's death follows the same rules as the owner's death
A verdict is finished only in the presence of the one being judged
A vaulted chamber where they are locked up

steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש, the argument in the משנה is only about oxen. חכמים compare an ox's trial to a person's trial and exempt all of them. רבי יהודה locks them in the כיפה.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: כְּמִיתַת בְּעָלִים כָּךְ מִיתַת הַשּׁוֹר,
phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: like the death of the owner, so is the death of the ox,
phrases.notes: Based on שמות 21:29, where the ox and its owner are spoken about together.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין גּוֹמְרִין דִּינוֹ שֶׁל שׁוֹר אֶלָּא בְּפָנָיו,
phrases.english: and they finish the verdict of an ox only in its presence,
therefore they are all exempt.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: כּוֹנְסִין אוֹתָן לַכִּיפָּה.
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds: they gather them into the vaulted chamber.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: כְּמִיתַת בְּעָלִים כָּךְ מִיתַת הַשּׁוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of both sides in the oxen case that ריש לקיש set up in step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חכמים: an ox is judged like its owner and needs its verdict in its presence, so all are exempt. רבי יהודה: they are locked in the כיפה.

steps.title: רבא begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a statement from רבא. His words continue in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only sets up the next move. רבא, the last name in the memory sign, is about to give a third answer to who the 'others' in the משנה are. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The content of רבא's statement comes in the text that follows. For now, only the name of the speaker is given.

phrases.english: Rava says:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces רבא, the last name in the סימן בשק״ר, who gives a third answer to the question of step 15 after שמואל and ריש לקיש. His words continue on the next amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. רבא's statement continues in the next part of the text.
